record.paper_title: Recent results on functional equations in a single variable, perspectives and open problems
record.original_question: Classify all continuous real-valued solutions φ:R→R of the functional equation φ(x + φ(x)) = φ(x)φ(x + 1). Segal's conjecture recorded in the paper asks whether the only continuous solutions are quadratic polynomials.

evidence.quote: Regarding solutions ϕ : R → R of (3.7) with k = 1: ϕ(x + ϕ(x)) = ϕ(x)ϕ(x + 1) (3.8) let us mention the paper [228] by S. L. Segal where, among others, the following conjecture is posed: The only continuous solutions ϕ : R → R of (3.8) are quadratic polynomials.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Classify all continuous functions φ: ℝ → ℝ satisfying the functional equation

    φ(x + φ(x)) = φ(x) · φ(x + 1)   for every x ∈ ℝ.

In particular, decide whether the only continuous solutions are the quadratic polynomials, i.e. functions of the form φ(x) = ax² + bx + c (with a, b, c ∈ ℝ) that satisfy the above identity, and if not, describe the complete set of continuous solutions.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a published resolution of Segal's conjecture concerning the continuous real-valued solutions of φ(x+φ(x)) = φ(x)φ(x+1). The conjecture is restated as open in recent surveys of functional equations in a single variable, and no counterexample or full classification appears to be available in the literature retrieved.

status_evidence.title: On a new class of functional equations satisfied by polynomial functions
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on polynomial functional equations does not include a resolution of the Segal equation φ(x+φ(x))=φ(x)φ(x+1).
status_evidence.claim: No published classification of continuous solutions of the Segal equation appears in recent functional-equation literature.
